newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end higher again with Enersis leading.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end higher again with Enersis leading.

text.p: Chilean shares, led by the Enersis energy group, surged for the third day in a row to close sharply higher in heavy trade, traders said.
The bull run is seen resuming Friday with the Enersis' rally giving momentum to the rest of the market, they said.
The selective index closed up 1.31 percent at 132.86 points. The general index firmed 0.63 percent to 5,706.81 points.
Turnover ballooned from 22 billion pesos Wednesday to 28 billion pesos -- the heaviest daily trade in over a month.
Enersis rose on media reports of strong first half earnings and of a resumption on talks on a possible alliance with Spanish utility Endesa, said brokers.

Newspaper El Mercurio reported that the company expected to first half net earnings of $163 million, or $1.19 per ADR, which is higher than the market consensus, said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
"My own calculations showed earnings of $1.03 but I give the report fairly high credence," said Hurd.
Traders said Enersis was also boosted by hopes the company will be successful in its bid to buy Brazilian state power distributor Coelba.
Enersis closed up 2.55 percent at 301 pesos. Subsidiary companies Endesa and Chilectra rose 2.42 percent to 317 pesos and 1.47 percent to 3,100 pesos, respectively.
Investment companies associated with Enersis, including Almendros and Chispa, also rose strongly.
Losers included holding company Quinenco, down 3.45 percent at 700 pesos and brewery CCU, which slipped 0.61 percent to 1,790 pesos.
